newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqis accused of spying for CIA shown on TV.
newsitem.headline: Iraqis accused of spying for CIA shown on TV.

text.p: Iraqi state television showed on Friday four Iraqis who confessed to spying for the U.S. Central Intelligence Agency (CIA).
Saad Daham Awad, 32, an officer in the Iraqi army, wore civilian dress and spoke in a relaxed manner to the television presenter.
Awad said he was recruited by the CIA to carry out espionage activities through a Kurd named Houker Ahmed Ali and his brother Haiman based in northern Iraq.
He said they worked with the agency's Iraq Trust group which works in northern Iraq under the cover of building hospitals.
He said Ali asked him to collect information on the Iraqi army and later on asked him also to recruit his brother Salah, who also appeared on the programme.
Awad said he started working with Ali smuggling medicine from Baghdad to the northern Kurdish region. This later developed into collecting information on the Iraqi army.
Two more confessed CIA spies also appeared on the programme.
